svg.title: Shared source and independent reselection give different two-item probabilities
svg.desc: Compare two procedures with source priors A two fifths and B three fifths, marked rates one fifth in A and one twentieth in B. First procedure: choose a single source once, then obtain two independent item results conditional on that source. The A route for two marked items has weight two fifths times one fifth squared, and the B route has weight three fifths times one twentieth squared. Adding them gives seven four-hundredths for both marked. Given the first item was marked, the probability that the second is marked is seven four-hundredths divided by eleven hundredths, or seven forty-fourths. Second procedure: independently choose a fresh source and take an item each time, with the same priors and rates. Each complete item procedure has marked probability eleven hundredths, and the two procedures are independent, so both marked has probability one hundred twenty-one ten-thousandths. Conditioning on the first marked result leaves the second probability eleven hundredths. The shared-source results are dependent for these priors and distinct rates, despite their specified conditional independence within either source.
